reasons.reader_question: The closing line makes the hidden-informant question specific: someone else inside the walls has stood at the warden's bed.
reasons.change: Muthu is exposed, stripped of the post-key and kept as captain. The raid plan is fixed, and Muthu is cleared of the guild leak.
reasons.romance_movement: For the first time Devan asks Neela about command and acts on her answer. The reason is new and earned by her guild knowledge.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Counting her bruise, her thumbnail rasp, the smudged gate and the 'don't make a habit' banter all show attraction without narration.
reasons.character_logic: A household rider reaching a sealed fort within two days of the arrest is implausible. Trusting Rema as a check on the crown's own informant goes unexamined.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Devan stakes the fort and his garrison on a known informant and names the cost aloud. Muthu takes the 'won't answer' like a blow.
reasons.prose: Clean, concrete and well varied, with no banned phrases. A few constructions are mannered ('It landed. Devan watched it land.').
reasons.continuity: 'Your mother wasn't in it. She's alive' makes Devan's dead mother alive. 'Eight years struck at air' ignores the Vellan blow and the ch5 spar.

fixes: Continuity: 'Your mother wasn't in it. She's alive' turns Devan's dead mother (bible, Janu) alive. Change it to 'My mother wasn't in it.' Also, 'For eight years he had struck at air and post and wall' ignores the Vellan blow (B1 ch27) and the light spar with Neela (B2 ch5). Rewrite it as 'Bar one blow in the Resin House yard and two touches with his wife, he had struck at air for eight years.'

Logic and continuity: in 'It came off post day. A rider, lathered, from the household', the timing cannot work. The pass was sealed, Kodiyur is four days away, and Ittan had been held only two days. Make the slip a standing order Muthu has carried since the ch23 off-day rider, to be used 'if the Keeper is ever held'. Also change 'who died on the road' to 'who died under the blackbark', which Muthu saw himself.

Character logic: 'He holds the fort for the man whose house he's guarded, and the crown's woman has the roll' leaves out that Devan knows the queen sealed his death. Rema is the crown's. Add one exchange where Neela asks why Rema's log protects him, and Devan cites Rema's written objection to the execution (B2 ch5) as proof she records against the crown. Also replace 'Gods, you're cold' with a non-deity oath, since the setting has no deities.
reader_question: If Muthu never wrote to the guild, who inside Kettamala has been close enough to the warden's chamber to tell them where Devan lays his sword?
new_facts_assessment: Muthu resealing the packet with his own grey stick is necessary and fits F429/F433. The letter's contents fit F286 except 'died on the road': Muthu found Ammu dead under the blackbark tree (F257, F408). The household rider bringing the slip conflicts with the sealed pass and Kodiyur being four days away (F208); the household could not have learned of the arrest in time.
